title: Wendell and the Tide
premise: Gideon Vane, once the most sought-after wedding planner on the coast, has spent three years hiding in small contracts and smaller towns since a scandal she didn't cause destroyed her career. When a legal quirk names her and her estranged childhood friend, orchard keeper Wendell Marsh, as co-owners of his family's failing vineyard and orchard, neither can sell without the other's signature. Forced to share one harvest season under one roof, they rebuild trust while uncovering that Gideon's old mentor orchestrated both her downfall and the deed itself to force a reckoning. In the end, they expose him at the harvest festival, choose each other over revenge, and sign the deed together—not to keep the land, but to give it away to the town that raised them.
about_author: Rosalind Delacroix is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade planning other people's perfect days before turning to fiction. She writes love stories about people who arrive too late, stay too long, and learn that timing is just another word for courage.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Hiding out planning a modest coastal wedding, Gideon receives certified papers naming her co-owner of Marsh Orchard alongside Wendell Marsh—the boy who never wrote back after she left town fifteen years ago. She plans to sign away her half by Friday. Emotional beat: guarded resignation masking old wounds.

chapters.title: A Man Made of Stone Fruit
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell refuses to sign; the orchard is the last thing holding his late mother's memory together, and he suspects the deed is a trap. He meets Gideon at the property line with a lawyer's letter and a basket of bruised peaches. Emotional beat: stubborn grief meeting prickly pride.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Neither will budge, so they strike an uneasy bargain: one season, shared labor, then mutual signatures. Gideon moves into the farmhouse's east wing. Their first week is all sharp edges—until she fixes his disaster of a harvest festival budget without being asked. Emotional beat: grudging respect taking root.

chapters.title: What the Deed Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Digging through county records, Wendell finds the deed was amended two years ago by a trust connected to Vivian Cross—Gideon's disgraced mentor. He says nothing, watching Gideon instead, torn between loyalty to the truth and fear of what it costs. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling into protectiveness.

chapters.title: Second Chances Are for People with Better Timing
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A storm traps them in the cider barn; Gideon finally tells the truth of her scandal—she took the fall for Vivian's forged client accounts. Wendell admits he never got her letters; his father burned them. The fifteen-year silence breaks open. Emotional beat: raw confession, first real intimacy.

chapters.title: The Vineyard's First Harvest Comes In
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Harvest begins in earnest; the town rallies around them, and Gideon feels the pull of belonging she'd sworn off. But Wendell's quiet digging surfaces: Vivian bought the deed deliberately, betting Gideon would flee again and forfeit her half. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by approaching threat.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Lie
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell confronts Gideon with the evidence—and with his own choice: expose Vivian and risk Gideon retreating behind her walls, or bury it and let her be free. She chooses truth, but insists on facing Vivian alone. They fight. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made flesh; painful rupture.

chapters.title: Everything Owed to the Tide
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon confronts Vivian in the city, offering testimony in exchange for leaving the orchard alone. Vivian counters with proof Wendell's father helped forge the original amendment—a secret that could break Wendell. Gideon must decide whose truth to carry home. Emotional beat: moral vertigo, sacrificial resolve.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Gideon returns and confesses everything, including Vivian's leverage. Wendell chooses her over his father's reputation; together they send the evidence to the press and the bar association instead of trading silence. At the empty station, Gideon asks him to ask her to stay. Emotional beat: climax of choice—truth chosen jointly, love declared plainly.

chapters.title: The Orchard Keeps What It Loves
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the harvest festival, the scandal breaks publicly and Gideon's name is cleared; the couple signs the deed transferring the orchard to a town land trust. Planning one last wedding—their own, small and imperfect—Gideon finally believes in them again. Emotional beat: found family, justice, and a hard-won homecoming.
